intro.heading: Points and ticks are how the market moves. P&L is what that movement means to you.
intro.body: Points are larger units of movement. Ticks are smaller pieces inside those points. P&L is the money attached to that movement once you add your instrument and contract count. This is the lesson where it stops being just chart language and starts becoming real.
intro.dayliNote: Bigger size makes the same move louder — the chart may be normal while your emotions are not. Staying small enough to stay teachable matters.

chart.heading: Watch P&L scale with contract size
chart.prompt: MNQ moves 30 points at $2/point. Tap a contract size to see the dollar result.

tapCards.prompt: MNQ moves 30 points and you hold 1 contract at $2/point. What's your P&L?

options.feedback: That's just the points, not multiplied by the point value.

tapCards.prompt: Same 30-point move, but now you're in 3 contracts instead of 1. What's the new P&L?

options.feedback: Right — 30 × $2 × 3 = $180. Same move, bigger size, bigger result.

tapCards.prompt: If 1 point = 4 ticks, and price moves 2 points against you on 1 MNQ contract, how many ticks did you lose?

options.label: 8 ticks
options.feedback: Right — 2 points × 4 ticks per point = 8 ticks.

quiz.question: If 1 point = 4 ticks, how many ticks are in 2 points?
A trader says "I made 30 points today" without mentioning contracts or instrument. Why is that statement incomplete?
options: Points alone don't tell you the dollar result — you also need the point value and contract count
It's a complete statement — points are all that matter
Points and dollars are always the same number
quiz.explanation: 30 points on MNQ at 1 contract is a very different dollar outcome than 30 points on MGC at 5 contracts.

quiz.question: P&L is calculated as points moved × point value × ___.
quiz.explanation: Contract count is the final multiplier that turns points into a real dollar result.
